_comment: This is the answer to 'if you pin a digest, how do you ever get updates?'
You don't hand-edit the digest. A bot opens a one-line PR, CI runs, you
review a diff you can actually read. Same idea as package-lock.json:
pinning does not mean frozen, it means updates are deliberate and visible.
Without this file, pinning a digest converts a moving base into a frozen,
un-patched one - which is worse than not pinning at all.

packageRules.description: Golden base images: group into one weekly PR and automerge digest-only bumps. A digest bump of an already-approved image is a STANDARD CHANGE - the golden image pipeline already gated it, so a second human review adds delay without adding assurance.
A MAJOR base image change (Python 3.14 -> 3.15) is a NORMAL CHANGE, not a digest bump. Never automerge: builder and runtime must move together or the venv's compiled extensions stop importing.
Python dependencies stay hash-pinned. Renovate must regenerate hashes, and they are per Python version - see requirements.txt.
GitHub Actions are pinned to SHAs. Keep the version comment in sync so the diff stays readable.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the weekly schedule. PCI-DSS 6.3.3 gives one month for critical patches; waiting for Monday burns a week of that for no reason.
